resources.string: Add a location to calculate prayer times.
Location permission is required for GPS.
Could not get a fix. Try again outdoors or enter coordinates.
Some skins cache the carrier label until SystemUI restarts.
PrayerBar writes the carrier label through Shizuku. No root needed.
Exact alarms are off — the label may update late.
Phone permission missing — grant it in Shizuku settings
Keeps the status bar label refreshed. Silence this channel to hide the sound; the notification itself is required by Android.
Keeping the status bar label up to date
While optimised, Android may kill the app when idle and the countdown stops refreshing on screen wake.
Optimised — the label can go stale after a long idle
Hold this notification to silence or minimise it
Android requires a visible notification for the background service that refreshes the countdown.
Blocked — the background service cannot show its notification
Time left until the next prayer
The tile is its own surface: its own text, its own switch, and no Shizuku needed. Tapping it does nothing.
Add it by hand from the Quick Settings edit screen.
Keep the tile up to date

Refreshes the tile in the background — at every prayer boundary, and every minute while the screen is on if it shows a countdown. Works with the carrier label switched off, but it needs the same ongoing notification to stay alive.
Quick Settings gives the tile two lines. Leave this empty to use just one.
Swaps the icon as the day moves on: a rising sun at dawn, a crescent at night.
The tile lights up in the system accent colour this long before the prayer. Off keeps it dim all day.

Android tints Quick Settings icons to match the system theme, so the per-prayer colour below is what you see in this app — on the panel itself it survives only on skins that skip that tint. The highlight above is the colour the platform does let an app control.
Next prayer, the countdown to it, and the rest of the day\'s times.
Long-press an empty spot on the home screen, pick Widgets, then PrayerBar. It resizes from 1x1 to 4x4 and rearranges itself at every size.
Your launcher cannot place widgets from inside an app. Long-press the home screen instead.
Which times the list holds. The countdown always points at the next tracked time, whether or not it is listed here. A small widget shows as many of these as fit, upcoming ones first.
Off leaves the next prayer\'s clock time as the headline.
Ticks every second, counted by the launcher itself rather than by a refresh — so it costs no extra battery.
How far the gap between the last time and the next one has run.
Dawn violet through to night blue. Off keeps one flat accent all day.
Fully transparent leaves only the text on the wallpaper.
Off pins the dark palette, which stays readable on a dark wallpaper under a light system theme.
Resize the widget on the home screen: 1x1 shows only the countdown, wider adds the clock time and the day\'s times, taller stacks them into a list.
Ongoing prayer status in the shade
The ongoing notification with the next prayer, the countdown to it and the day\'s times. Silence or hide this channel to switch it off from the system side.
This is the pulled-open shape. Collapsed, the shade keeps the header, the two lines and the bar.

PrayerBar already has to show one notification while it refreshes in the background, so this takes that slot over rather than adding a second one — with the status on, the mandatory notice becomes the status. It sits in a channel of its own, apart from the plain one.
The line under the title. It still refreshes on the minute while the screen is on.
Ticks down every second in the corner where the time usually sits. Android counts it itself, so it costs no battery.
How far the gap between the last time and the next one has run.
Paints the whole notification in the prayer colour instead of tinting only the icon. Only an ongoing notification is allowed this.
Listed when the notification is pulled open, the next one in bold. The shade draws six lines, so a longer list drops the times already called.
Leave it empty to name the place after the town it falls in.
The label as status bar icons
Spells the label out beside the system icons. Needs Shizuku.

The bar fits about %1$d icons. A countdown like 1:45 is drawn in one piece and takes a single one; anything else costs one per character. A label too wide is collapsed into a single dot by the system.
No glyph for %1$s — dropped from the label.
Shizuku is not connected, so nothing can be written to the status bar.
The system drops these icons on reboot. PrayerBar puts them back as it starts.
